transcript.text: This is Swift, an automated flood assistant working with local emergency services. Am I speaking with someone at 156 Unnamed Rd?
Yeah, this is me at 156 Unnamed Rd, just me here, no one else, water’s not in the house, and I’m totally fine—no need for any truck, boat, or help, I’m good on my own.
Thanks for confirming you’re okay and not needing help. How many people are at the home right now, including anyone who can't come to the phone?
Just me here, all good, no one else around, and I’m totally fine on my own—no need for a truck, boat, or any seats, water’s not even inside!
Is there anyone there who can't leave on their own, for example someone who uses a wheelchair, needs oxygen, or is bedbound? If it's a wheelchair, does it have a motor?
No one here can’t leave on their own, and I’m the only person—no wheelchair, no oxygen, nothing like that, just me, and I’m fine, no water inside either.
Is there water inside the home right now?
No, there’s no water inside at all, just me here by myself, and I’m totally fine, no need for any help or equipment—everything’s dry and safe.
If neighbors need a ride out, do you have a high-clearance truck, a boat, or free seats in a vehicle?
Nope, I’m all good here—just me, no water inside, and I don’t have a truck, boat, or any spare seats to lend out.
Thanks for letting us know you’re all good here. Let me read that back: people at the home not confirmed; no water inside yet. Is that right?
Yeah, that’s right—just me here, no water in yet, and I’m totally fine, no need for help or anything.
Thanks for confirming you’re okay and no water’s in yet. I've recorded that everyone there can leave on their own. Don't drive through flooded roads. Turn around, don't drown. Goodbye.
